Resolves #21603
Related: #21198, #21033

Opening Mail starts an animation from its launcher icon into an 880 × 520 desktop window. The header’s **Pop out window** button already accepts a click or Enter during that animation. On the v14 candidate, activating it early opened an icon-sized popup. The inbox was too small to select another message.

`AppWindow#popOutWindow()` now awaits an existing mount flight before measuring the source. It rechecks visibility, ownership and the source window ID before continuing. A settled dialog takes its usual path. The drag gesture, native-vessel transport and popup reload lifecycle retain their existing code.

Evidence: L3 (trusted Enter at the measured launcher geometry, real Chrome popup rectangle, message selection and return; Firefox and WebKit controls) → L3 required. The [release steward’s bounded-fix exception](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21033#issuecomment-7093446376) and [physical-test handoff](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21603#issuecomment-7090893887) apply.

## AC Evidence

| Acceptance | Result |
| --- | --- |
| An early header activation uses the settled geometry | On `aa41c1f139` the real branded-Chrome test failed at **100 × 96** versus the expected **880 × 520**. With the source fix the same initial Enter opened one correctly sized popup. The test checks the actual trusted activation against the measured launcher, then selects Robin Chen’s message and returns to the original task. |
| Existing behavior | All six Web Desktop Apps browser cases passed three times with retries disabled (**18/18**). The normal app sizes, Calendar, Recycle Bin, phone bounds and popup revocation checks also passed. |
| Scope and handoff | Five executable lines are confined to the header path. Sophie, the original issue owner, independently reproduced the source failure and the repaired interaction. Site acceptance includes the operator’s real mouse/focus test. |

## Deltas from ticket

The original tear-out shipped to `dev` in [#22067](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/22067). Sophie reopened the implementation lane with Emmy for the sizing defect found during release testing. The repair preserves the pending-activation latch and the source lifetime checks across the extra await.

## Test Evidence

`npm run test-e2e -- test/playwright/e2e/webdesktop/Apps.spec.mjs --workers=1 --retries=0 --repeat-each=3` passed on the repair. The new browser case controls the timing of the normal expansion delta, releases it on the dialog’s own header event and restores the test fixture on all exits.

In the production-build WebKit comparison, three early clicks opened an unusable 100 × 96 popup on the candidate base and one usable 880 × 520 popup on each repaired run. Firefox admitted the repaired early pointer and keyboard activations with popup blocking enabled. Signing out while the activation waited left no popup or task. The next normal Mail launch succeeded.

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** contained — one guard in `AppWindow#popOutWindow` plus its e2e; no API or contract change.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** Before measuring, the pop-out now waits for the dialog's own `mountFlight`. That is the engine's latch for an animated show (`startMountFlight(#afterAnimation(animateShow()))`, `component/Base.mjs:2045`), and it clears itself when the animation settles. After the wait, the method re-checks `#canPopOut` and `windowId` in the same way as the check that already followed the measurement. The early `return false` still passes through `finally`, so `#popOutPending` clears. Verified on `35369860cf`: the new e2e passes, and with the five lines removed it fails with a 100 × 96 popup against the expected 880 × 520, so it is red on dev and green on the head (run locally). Hosted CI is green. What I looked for was whether the wait could outlive the popup's transient activation. It adds at most the ~283 ms opening animation, well inside Chrome's activation window. WebKit's shorter window is covered only by the Firefox and WebKit controls the PR names, not by my run, and the operator's physical test at ~10:00 UTC is the final read. The PR meets all four conditions of the hold amendment (#21033 `issuecomment-7093446376`): it is bounded, it has a red/green e2e, it has a cross-family approval with this review, and it can merge before that test.

**Findings:** None.
